PMID:41322931.topic: Ottawa ankle rules in radiograph requests
PMID:41322931.setting: Emergency department, Newham University Hospital (district general hospital, East London)
PMID:41322931.standard: Royal College of Radiologists: 100% of ankle plain-film requests for trauma should reference the Ottawa Ankle Rules

cycle1.result: 37/100 (37%) requests referenced the OAR. 21 (21%) fractures; 13 (61.9%) of these requests documented the OAR and 8 (38.1%) did not (P = 0.011).

PMID:41322931.intervention: Findings presented at clinical governance meetings; focused education sessions for front-line clinicians and targeted briefings for radiographers who vet X-ray requests.

cycle2.result: 51/100 (51%) requests referenced the OAR (P = 0.046). 31 (31%) fractures; 26 (83.9%) had OAR documented and 5 (16.1%) did not (P < 0.001).

PMID:41322931.other_findings: Compliance remained well below the 100% RCR target. Authors suggest electronic OAR prompts in request systems and induction teaching for rotating doctors.

PMID:38783183.setting: Debre Tabor Comprehensive Specialized Hospital; elective general, orthopaedic and gynaecological surgery
PMID:38783183.standard: NICE guideline on routine preoperative tests for elective surgery

cycle1.result: 350 investigations requested; 71 (20.28%) ordered without justification or against NICE recommendations (about 79.71% in line). FBC requested in 240 (97.16%); inappropriate FBC in 45 patients, ECG in 5, urinalysis in 4, hemostasis in 1, CXR in 1. Indicated PT/PTT not done in 4 and HbA1c not done in 4.

PMID:38783183.other_findings: No patient tested without a clear indication had an abnormal result. Authors recommend an accessible institutional guideline and regular re-audit.

PMID:29755914.setting: Paediatric orthopaedic department, Royal Hospital for Children, Glasgow
PMID:29755914.standard: UK national guidelines: displaced supracondylar fractures treated by early surgical stabilisation with bicortical wire fixation; bi-columnar fixation assessed on intra-operative AP radiograph

cycle1.dates: June 2014 to December 2016 (methods state April 2014 to December 2016)
cycle1.result: Bi-columnar fixation achieved in 41/49 (84%): 7/7 (100%) cross-wire cases and 34/42 (81%) lateral-entry-only cases. Intra-articular wire in 44/49 (90%). Loss of fixation needing revision 1/49 (2%), in a case without bi-columnar fixation (1/8, 13%).

PMID:29755914.other_findings: One superficial infection (2%) and no deep infection or septic arthritis. Bi-columnar fixation rates varied widely between the nine surgeons (60% to 100%); a re-audit is planned.

PMID:41141882.topic: Patient information leaflet delivery in fracture clinic
PMID:41141882.setting: Fracture clinic and trauma triage, Leicester Royal Infirmary, University Hospitals of Leicester
PMID:41141882.standard: Green Surgery Report (UKHACC 2023) sustainability aims; local success target of at least 50% of patients preferring QR code leaflets and at least 30% cost and carbon reduction

cycle1.result: 31 (62%) reported reading printed leaflets; 38 (76%) preferred digital/QR code information; 45 (90%) owned a smartphone. All patients aged 80 or over preferred printed leaflets.

PMID:41141882.intervention: QR codes created for six commonly used leaflets; consolidated QR poster in consultation rooms and triage; change communicated to staff by email and meetings.

cycle2.result: 16 (80%) familiar with QR codes and able to save the leaflet; 13 (65%) preferred QR codes, 4 (20%) paper, 3 (15%) either. Estimated annual saving over £1600 and about 252 kg CO2.

PMID:41141882.other_findings: Preference for digital leaflets was strongly associated with younger age; older patients needed printed copies, so a hybrid approach is advised.

PMID:40702969.setting: Trauma and orthopaedic department, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust (acute teaching hospital)
PMID:40702969.standard: Locally designed trauma meeting documentation standards (no UK guideline exists); record keeping guidance from GMC, RCS England and BMA

cycle1.result: 58/90 (64%) had some documentation. Consultant on call 43%, other consultants 29%, imaging 20%, MDT concerns 7%, diagnosis 29%, laterality 22%, clear plan 63%, weight-bearing 1%.

PMID:40702969.intervention: Electronic trauma meeting proforma (EPR shortcut) introduced, then revised after MDT feedback (theatre checklist added); teaching video and poster for new doctors before the one-year re-audit.

cycle2.result: 71/85 (84%) had some documentation. Consultant on call, other consultants and imaging 100%, diagnosis 97%, laterality 75%, clear plan 98%.

PMID:40702969.other_findings: Phase 2 (11 to 20 October 2022, n=98) reached 94% documentation; phase 3 (20 to 30 October 2022, n=108) 88%, with only 6/57 (11%) completing the new theatre checklist. Weight-bearing and MDT concerns sections were later removed.

PMID:35470389.setting: 62 centres in 16 countries (INTELLECT collaborative, multicentre retrospective audit)
PMID:35470389.country: International (16 countries, 1045 patients from the UK)

cycle1.result: Median time to antibiotics 2 h (1–5); wound debridement within 24 h in 80.2%; median time to debridement 10 h (4–20); consultant-led debridement 80%; orthopaedic and plastic joint debridement 14%. Wound infection 16.3%, deep infection 10.3%, non-union 10.9%.

PMID:35470389.other_findings: Treatment in settings with national guidelines was protective against deep infection (OR 0.66) and non-union (OR 0.66); soft tissue closure beyond 72 h was linked to infection, non-union and amputation, and joint ortho-plastic care protected against secondary amputation (OR 0.41).

PMID:41962925.setting: 53 UK NHS hospitals including 8 major trauma centres (national trainee-led collaborative, CURFFED)
PMID:41962925.standard: BOAST Early Management of the Paediatric Forearm Fracture (2021)

cycle1.result: Mean overall BOAST compliance 63% (42.5% to 86.9%). Pain scores 83 (20%); regular analgesia 372 (87%); complete pre-manipulation NV assessment 214 (50%), post-manipulation 147 (35%); consent 163 (38%); analgesia and advice on discharge complete 95 (23%); consultant review within 48 h 328 (78%); clinic within 7 days 238 (59%). 423/577 (73%) manipulated first in ED.

PMID:41962925.other_findings: Median time to first manipulation 2 h 43 min in ED versus 18 h 47 min in theatre. Only 9 of 53 sites supplied a local protocol and 8 a patient information leaflet.

PMID:41416288.standard: BOAST ankle fracture guidance (weight-bearing as tolerated after stable fixation) and WAX trial (weight-bearing from two weeks)

cycle1.result: First weight-bearing at 2 weeks 2/42 (4.8%), 2–6 weeks 9/42 (21.4%), over 6 weeks 31/42 (73.8%) (6–8 weeks 21/42, 50.0%; over 8 weeks 10/42, 23.8%). Median 48 days (IQR 42–56); none discharged weight-bearing as tolerated.

PMID:41416288.other_findings: Early safety was reassuring (unplanned contact 1/42, no re-operations or loss of reduction, delayed union 2/42). Posterior malleolus fixation was linked to longer time to weight-bearing (p=0.036); re-audit planned at 6–9 months after a default WBAT-from-two-weeks pathway.

PMID:39066677.setting: 43 centres in 13 countries (INTELLECT paediatric subgroup, multicentre retrospective audit)
PMID:39066677.country: International (13 countries, 66 patients from the UK)

cycle1.result: Median time to antibiotics 2 h; median time to primary wound excision 11 h; combined orthopaedic and plastic surgery care from debridement in 14%; consultant-led excision 71%. Wound infection 20 (12%), deep infection 8 (5%), non-union 9 (6%).

PMID:39066677.other_findings: Soft tissue closure beyond 72 h was associated with soft tissue infection (OR 14.67); children aged 5 or under had more deep infection (OR 16.89). About one-third of cases needing reconstruction were Gustilo IIIB/IIIC.

PMID:39205710.setting: Regional orthopaedic unit, emergency trauma cases, Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust
PMID:39205710.standard: BOAST safe use of intraoperative tourniquets: documented skin checks, isolation, exsanguination, pressure (SBP-based) and time; ischaemic time under 120 minutes

cycle1.result: Full adherence 3 (6.0%), partial 16 (32.0%), overall compliance 38.0%; not adhered 31 (62.0%).

PMID:39205710.intervention: After EPR introduction: survey, department emails and theatre posters; then findings presented at audit meeting and an EPR smart phrase template with drop-downs and automatic SBP calculation introduced.

cycle2.result: Full adherence 9 (18.0%), partial 22 (44.0%), overall compliance 62.0% (p=0.0005 vs 17.0% in cycle 2). Pressure documented 76%, time 94%, skin pre 56%, post 60%, isolation 60%, exsanguination 24%; pressure within standard 24 (63.1%).

PMID:39205710.other_findings: An intermediate cycle after EPR roll-out (June to July 2023, n=59) fell to 17.0% compliance with 0% skin and isolation documentation. Only 44% of 50 surgeons surveyed knew the BOAST guidance; mean lower limb pressure fell from 287.06 to 265.91 mmHg (p=0.007).

PMID:32821186.topic: Preoperative anaemia screening before joint replacement
PMID:32821186.setting: Four campuses (three private, one public) of a tertiary metropolitan healthcare facility, South East Queensland; primary total hip and knee replacement
PMID:32821186.standard: National Blood Authority Patient Blood Management guidelines: FBC, iron studies, CRP and renal function at least 6 weeks before surgery, with treatment of anaemia

cycle1.result: FBC 96% (583), renal 94.7% (575/607), iron studies 8% (49/607), CRP 2.4% (15); all recommended tests 2.4% (15). Screening 6 weeks or more before surgery 3.95% (24/607). 85 (14.6%) anaemic; 10/85 had some preoperative treatment and 1.2% (n = 1) received guideline-concordant treatment.

PMID:32821186.other_findings: Anaemic patients were more likely to be transfused (OR 8.65) and stayed one day longer; 21/40 (52.5%) transfusion episodes did not follow PBM guidance. A standardised anaemia pathway was being developed.

PMID:34227969.topic: Mental health of shielded children during COVID-19
PMID:34227969.setting: Children aged 2–17 registered with GP practices contributing to the SAIL databank, Wales (data linkage study)
PMID:34227969.other_findings: Not an audit: a data linkage study showing anxiety or depression diagnoses or prescriptions fell during COVID-19, with new diagnoses higher in shielded children (2.0%) than the general population (1.0%).

cycle1.result: Most patients followed a late weight-bearing protocol; early weight-bearing was used in younger patients with lower BMI. No differences in union, complications or length of stay; fracture-related infection 1 (4%) vs 5 (2.5%), EWB vs LWB (P=0.922).

PMID:39366631.other_findings: Average cost of surgical management €6,419, driven mainly by length of stay; total costs did not differ between early and late weight-bearing. All open fractures followed late weight-bearing.
